claims.text: Answer: on the three sampled land tiles the Imperial and War eras differ from Modern only in colour (a land-hue recolour), not in roads, rivers, coast, forest or lettering. The linework (dotted roads, solid rivers, coastline, ring-dot settlements, hand lettering) sits at the same pixels in all three eras, so 'dead roads' and 'forest that grew back' are NOT carried by tiles-imperial/ or tiles-war/.

evidence.ref: tile-diff over maps-site/{tiles,tiles-imperial,tiles-war}/5/{11/11,9/11,10/12}.jpg (PIL/numpy/scipy: ink-mask match, affine/LUT colour-fit residual, gradient correlation)

claims.text: Raw pixel difference is large but is a tint, not structure: mean abs RGB diff Modern vs Imperial is 10.7 / 14.4 / 17.4 (tiles 11/11, 9/11, 10/12) and Modern vs War 9.9 / 13.5 / 16.0, with 68-99.9% of pixels byte-different (JPEG re-encode included). Mean RGB moves from about (176,162,120) to (180,146,108) on 11/11: land turns terracotta/salmon (R-B on land about 66 to about 95) while sea stays grey-green.

evidence.ref: mean|A-B| per tile and per-era mean RGB, same script as q14-c01

claims.text: Ink geometry is unchanged. A local-contrast ink mask (luminance 45 below its 25px box mean) gives 5562 / 5474 / 5465 ink px on 11/11 (Modern / Imperial / War), 6396 / 6275 / 6253 on 9/11, 3218 / 3148 / 3147 on 10/12. In every pairwise direction (Modern<->Imperial, Modern<->War, Imperial<->War) 100.0% of ink px of one era lie within 2 px of ink in the other. Connected-component counts match (74/74/74, 111/112/112, 33/34/34; the +-1 is threshold splitting). Ink IoU is 0.97-0.98 Modern vs era and 0.99 Imperial vs War.

evidence.ref: ink-mask IoU and 2px-dilation agreement, same script as q14-c01

claims.text: Structure correlation is near 1 across eras: edge-map correlation Modern vs Imperial 0.9948 / 0.9944 / 0.9952 and Modern vs War 0.9944 / 0.9939 / 0.9950 (11/11, 9/11, 10/12); gradient-magnitude correlation on 11/11 is 0.998. A per-channel affine fit Modern->Imperial leaves mean residual 3.7 / 3.8 / 1.3 grey levels; a pooled 16-level RGB colour lookup leaves 3.3 / 3.4 / 2.0, concentrated at light label halos and coast edges rather than in new features.

evidence.ref: np.lstsq 3x3+offset fit and quantised-RGB LUT residual, same script

claims.text: Eyeball check of 2x side-by-side crops of all three tiles: same coast, same dotted road network (e.g. Sokundo to the east on 11/11, the LAMO/ Epeshu-side roads on 9/11), same solid river lines, same settlement ring-dots, same lettering (Sokundo, Aldorus, Reketis, Pharzeban, the spaced region letters). No glyph, spelling or road difference is visible, and no forest glyphs exist in any era on these tiles. A 4x crop of the Sokundo label shows identical letterforms, only the pale halo and nearby land colour change.

evidence.ref: maps-site/tiles/5/11/11.jpg px 60,30,180,80 and full 256x256 of 11/11, 9/11, 10/12 in the three eras (side-by-sides at 512 px)

claims.text: Imperial and War are the same recolour at two strengths: they differ by a red-channel offset only. On land pixels War is about 6.5 lower in R than Imperial on all three tiles (6.52 / 6.70 / 6.51) with G and B within 0.35; Imperial vs War mean abs diff is only 1.9 / 2.6 / 2.8 and max 23-29, with 0% of pixels differing by more than 24. Their ink masks match with IoU 0.989-0.993.

evidence.ref: imp-war channel means on land (R-B>80) pixels, same script

claims.text: The three era pyramids are structurally parallel: tiles/, tiles-imperial/ and tiles-war/ each hold 860 jpg tiles, and the repo history shows they were produced together as one sharpened z0-5 set (2x LANCZOS + unsharp) in the same commits, with no separate era artwork or era source maps in the repo.

evidence.ref: find maps-site/<dir> -name '*.jpg' | wc -l == 860 each; git commits 090f971 and dfbf5f0 (v0.6.1-alpha.1: 'Sharpened z5 pyramids ... for Modern, Imperial, and War of the Patrons')

claims.text: In the shipped atlas the era control is a pure base-layer swap with no era-dependent labels, borders or names: setEra removes one L.tileLayer and adds another and writes no hash; the radios are 'Modern (1374 A.B.)', 'War of the Patrons (1124-1133)', 'Imperial (the golden age)'. All name and border content lives in separate overlays that do not change with era.

The open question the research dossier recorded is now resolved on land tiles: it noted tiles are 'byte-different' and that a sampled ocean tile looked the same by eye, with a land side-by-side outstanding. Byte-difference is explained by the recolour; the brief's 'dead roads, old spellings, forest that grew back' cannot be delivered by swapping to the existing era rasters.

Consequence for R14 and 'old survey under the live sheet': the existing era rasters can only serve as a tint/atmosphere layer (a stacked or swiped base at opacity/swipe). The 'old names / dead roads / regrown forest' content has to come from a new authored layer (an old-name layer built from lexicon etymology via the Patrinaic roots tool and tools/build-gazetteer.js, plus authored dead-road and forest-regrowth vectors), per the R14 wording that an old-name layer is needed when the eras differ only in names.

evidence.ref: docs/filigree/README.md :: an era tile layer stacked under the live base (opacity/swipe); an old-name layer too if the eras differ only in names

gaps: Only 3 z5 land tiles were compared; roads/forest/names were not checked on other tiles, other zooms (z0-4) or any tile near Lepon, Epeshu or the mountain ranges where an era-specific edit would most likely sit.

Whether the eras differ in political BORDERS or names was only checked as drawn lettering and linework on these three tiles; the solid lines here are rivers per the cartographic key, and no political border line is identifiable on them, so borders in the eras are not established either way.

Ink identity was measured by a luminance mask within 2 px; a tiny stroke added or removed below that scale (or a faint non-ink hatch) would not be detected, and no forest glyph exists in the Modern tiles to compare against.
No era source maps (PatrinorImperial/War originals) exist in the repo, so how the era pyramids were produced is inferred from pixels and two commit messages, not from a script.

The 100% within-2px ink agreement is a stricter statement than the +-1 component-count differences suggest; the +-1 components were attributed to threshold splitting but their exact location was not inspected.
summary: On the three sampled land tiles (z5 11/11, 9/11, 10/12) the Imperial and War eras are a pure land-hue recolour of Modern: dotted roads, rivers, coast, settlements and lettering match pixel-for-pixel (100% of ink within 2 px, edge correlation about 0.995), and no forest or dead-road content exists in any era. War differs from Imperial only by a roughly 6.5-level lower red channel on land. So 'old survey under' as a raster swap gives only tint; old names, dead roads and regrown forest need a new authored layer.
